text:
maya: Quick sync — we have the OSS "LiteKit" bundle ready in the repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/litekit). Need a short launch post, a compact benchmark narrative for the docs, a 30-min webinar plan, and inbound routing for dev leads. Who can own which piece?

oliver: I can take launch post + social copy. Will draft microblog + 2 tweets. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sanjay: I’ll own the benchmark narrative. Want to highlight latency/cost tradeoffs and a small sample: hosted API vs local quantized run. Short table and 3 charts. Need test vectors.

emily: I can do webinar planning — 30-minute hands-on demo targeting devs curious about low-cost inference. Proposed outline: 5m intro, 12m demo (refapp walkthrough), 8m benchmarks & Q/A, 5m next steps. Speaker: Sanjay for benchmarks, Oliver for product overview, me for demo.

jin: For inbound routing — we should map the registration form to Intercom + HubSpot. Small question: do we want a separate routing for enterprise-tagged leads (SLA/private) vs community? My suggestion: enterprise -> sales queue (priority), community -> marketing nurture.

maya: yep that routing sounds right. Also add a UTM scheme so we can track which content piece drove signups (utm_source=oss-litekit, utm_medium=social|webinar|post).

oliver: Draft social copy (first pass):
```
Launch thread: "Introducing LiteKit — a compact, open inference reference for building cost-efficient LLM features. Demo + benchmarks + starter code. Try the repo: github.com/redwood-inference/litekit"
Tweet variants: short CTA + link, one with benchmark hook: "3x cheaper per token on typical chat loads vs default setup" (we'll validate).
```

emily: For the webinar landing page I'll put the agenda + 1-click calendar adds. Need a hero screenshot (suggest demo UI) and 2 bullets: "Start in minutes" and "Cost/latency comparison".

sanjay: Benchmarks plan: run 3 scenarios — hosted API (redwood-hosted), Dedicated small GPU (T4-equivalent), local quantized (4-bit llama-style). Metrics: median p95 latency at 128 tokens, cost per 1k tokens (approx), and model quality sanity-check (perplexity on prompt set). Will commit results and short narrative. ETA 48 hrs.

jin: For routing I'll use a lightweight Zap: Typeform -> HubSpot + Intercom. HubSpot field mapping: email, company, country, interest (oss-litekit/webinar/refapp). Also mark a boolean field "enterprise_interest" if company domain matches list. Intercom: create a lead with tag "oss-litekit" and assign to SDR rotation if enterprise_interest=true.

maya: Perfect. Also we should prepare 1 short dev tutorial (10–15 min) that can be embedded in the post and linked in the webinar. Oliver — can you pick 3 endpoints to demo (text-gen, embeddings, rerank)?

oliver: Yes — text-gen (chat), embeddings (semantic search example), and a tiny reranker for results. I'll make a step-by-step quickstart and a runnable Colab.

emily: Webinar logistics: target date = next Thursday 11am PT. I'll book Zoom + Record + autopublish to youtube. Marketing-bot — please reserve calendar and create a registration page.

marketing-bot: Created event draft: "LiteKit: hands-on demo for devs" on 1709977200. Registration page URL: https://redwood.com/events/litekit-demo (draft).

maya: Nice. Also need a short benchmark narrative blurb for the post: 2–3 sentences emphasizing predictable inference economics and easy startup. Sanjay, can you give two callouts: (1) cost delta for common chat workloads; (2) example configuration that reduced p95 by X%? Keep numbers conservative.

sanjay: Will do. Example callouts (placeholder until runs): "~2–3x cost improvement using prefix caching + 4-bit quantization on common chat traces" and "p95 reduced ~20% using our batching/serve config vs naive single-request". I'll confirm numbers before publish.

jin: One more: lead scoring rule idea — anyone registering for the webinar + clicks pricing page -> score +10. If company domain in enterprise list -> score +30 and auto-assign to SDR. Thoughts?

maya: Good. Let's keep the scoring conservative to avoid false positives. Jin, add the rule but don't auto-add to the enterprise nurture until we manually validate top 5 leads after the first event.

oliver: I'm drafting post now. Two headline options:
- "LiteKit: an opinionated starting kit for inference that doesn't break the bank"
- "Build fast, cheap LLM features — meet LiteKit"
Which one?

maya: Second feels more action-oriented. Go with that. Keep post length ~250–350 words. Include 1 GIF of the demo and the Colab link.

emily: I'll create the slide deck template and record a dry run for 20 mins on Tue. Can everyone be available for a quick run-through Tue 9am PT?

all: +1 / available.

oliver: Quick ask — can someone drop a short checklist for prepublish (assets)? I can start: 1) hero screenshot, 2) GIF, 3) colab link, 4) benchmark charts, 5) social copy, 6) landing page.

maya: I'll make a small Notion checklist and share. Also, tagging legal for the OSS license blurb — @jin can you add license note in the repo README?

jin: Will add LICENSE = Apache-2.0 and short attribution.

sanjay: After I finish runs I'll push a small artifacts folder with CSVs + PNG charts and a one-paragraph analysis to the repo under /benchmarks/summary.md.

oliver: Great. I'll sync social schedule once we have final numbers. If anything blocks, ping me here. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Release pipeline note: docs site deploy scheduled when PR #412 merges. CI checks must pass.

maya: Cool team — action owners: Oliver (post + social), Sanjay (benchmarks), Emily (webinar + slides), Jin (routing + license), Maya (overall coordination). We'll reconvene Tue morning after dry run. Thanks! :tada:
